CHROMIUM: iwl7000: mvm: disable TX-AMSDU on older NICs On older NICs, we occasionally see issues with A-MSDU support, where the commands in the FIFO get confused and then we see an assert EDC because the next command in the FIFO isn't TX. We've tried to isolate this issue and understand where it comes from, but haven't found any errors in building the A-MSDU in software. At least for now, disable A-MSDU support on older hardware so that users can use it again without fearing the assert. This fixes https://bugzilla.kernel.org/show_bug.cgi?id=203315. py/device: Support motion sensor setup for gyroscope We used to create a GyroscopeGroup for a complete gyroscope test cycle, which includes: - motion sensor setup - calibration - main gyro test Setting sensor is mandatory before running any gyroscope relating test, but the setup command is not properly supported and we need to add it manually into test list, which makes things tedious and error prone. In addition, though ectool provides gyroscope information, we were not leveraging that to provide functionalities e.g. parameter checking or auto adaption. This CL tries to add some supports for that in gyroscope.py so pytests can call SetupMotionSensor() to set it up, and if the needed parameters like ID or frequency are not provided as arguments, help functions will collect the information from ectool and try to automatically fill the blanks up. CRAS: hfp_info - Read HCI SCO header for packet staus flag BT adapter has erroneous data reporting mechanism to tell if each HCI SCO packet contains intact payload, and this information lives in the HCI SCO header. With kernel SCO module configured to send up HCI SCO packet with header, CRAS can incorporate the status flag to help detect packet loss. With the help of erroneous data reporting, change the size of read buffer to one HCI SCO packet, We no longer expect valid data would live across two packets. Even with erroneous data reporting, we shall keep all checks for cases where mSBC frame could not be found or decoded, and error log them because that means false positive in erroneous data reporting. BUG=chromium:980454 TEST=Manual test BT recording with Sony WH-1000XM3 headset.
